_comment: PROPOSED colourway names, awaiting the owner's approval — applied by scripts/publish-garment.mjs.
Every name and hex here was MEASURED out of the 2026-09-03 diffuse-off CLO exports by
fabricsByVariant + the CIEDE2000 palette in colour-name.ts, not typed by hand. A name is
compound ("Wine / Black") where a SECOND fabric covers 18% or more of the colourway's
fabric area, which is the shape both live products already use in the CMS.
THE slug IS THE IRREVERSIBLE FIELD. It becomes part of the URL printed on that garment's
QR tag, so once a tag exists it can never change. deltaE is the palette distance: above 10
the match is weak and the robot itself refused to guess, leaving the CMS row blank.
The two live products are deliberately absent: their names are already set and still match
their files.
ADDED 2026-09-07: the five garments from that day's exports (r-cch, r-gtd, r-au, r-ect,
r-et). Same method, measured on the RAW exports with fabricsByVariant. Four names the
robot left blank were chosen by the owner from labelled renders; one — r-ect Colorway 4 —
was named "Beige" CONFIDENTLY and wrongly (the garment is pale sage green), so it was
renamed and its slug moved off /beige while the product was still an unpublished draft.
That is the 2026-08-03 failure in miniature: a confident wrong name beats a blank one only
if the arithmetic and the picture agree. LOOK AT THE RENDER.
ADDED 2026-09-27: the 24 garments processed on the owner's Mac (scripts/process-local.mjs, which
applies these words BEFORE the colour import, so a slug is never the sampler's guess). The owner
delegated the colour words ("my QR codes point at the garment only, so you choose"). Each name was
chosen by LOOKING at a front render of that colourway beside CLO's own render where one exists;
`hex` is the fabric colour measured off the file and `robotName` the palette's nearest word, kept
for the record. The sampler read two garments (r-kmj, r-mss) as "Black #000000" on all five
colourways at high confidence — see withNamePlan in scripts/process-local-lib.mjs.
